brief: Four Goldman desk notes argue credit's calm response to Thursday's post-midterm equity rout is masking AI risk shifting down the supply chain. The selloff erased $2.5 trillion of Nasdaq value, but CDX IG widened only 3.5bps and CDX HY moved far less than its historical beta to equities implied over the week. A technical bid for 'boring' paper absorbed record IG issuance ($76bn last week, $2.079tn YTD, hyperscalers alone pricing $67bn across five deals). Underneath, a basket of chip CDS (Broadcom, AMD, Nvidia, Intel) traded wider than a basket of hyperscaler CDS (Oracle, SpaceX, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft) for the first time in three months, roughly doubling since August, while hyperscalers shortened tenors and tapped euro markets for cheaper funding. In HY, data-center bonds sold off sharply on regulatory risk (40 of 41 local ballot measures went against data centers), and distressed credit (triple-Cs, leveraged loans) is deteriorating even as the index holds. One trader, Biswas, frames this as rising uncertainty rather than rising risk and stays net long IG carry while shorting HY versus iTraxx financials. Goldman still forecasts spreads widening into December, overshooting March's wides.
